cd LlamaFactory
pip install -e .
pip install -r requirements/metrics.txt

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: LlamaFactory is a toolkit for fine-tuning more than 100 large language models with a command line or a web UI and little or no code. It supports LoRA, QLoRA, full fine-tuning, DPO, PPO and more for models like Qwen, LLaMA, Mistral, DeepSeek and Gemma.
sixtySeconds.problem: Fine-tuning usually means writing training scripts and wiring libraries together for each model. LlamaFactory puts many models and methods behind YAML configs, a three-command workflow and a Gradio web interface called LLaMA Board.
whoFor: Developers fine-tuning open models on their data
Teams without deep ML engineering resources
Users of NVIDIA, AMD or Ascend NPU hardware
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for broad model and method coverage with a zero-code UI. You still need a suitable GPU; the README's table estimates 6 GB for 4-bit QLoRA on a 7B model.
requirements: A GPU with enough memory (CUDA 11.6+, or AMD ROCm, or Ascend NPU)

overview: LlamaFactory supports many model families, including LLaMA, LLaVA, Mistral, Mixtral, Qwen3, Qwen3-VL, DeepSeek, Gemma, GLM and Phi. Methods include continued pre-training, supervised fine-tuning (including multimodal), reward modelling, PPO, DPO, KTO and ORPO.

Training can be 16-bit full or freeze tuning, LoRA, or QLoRA at 2 to 8 bits through several quantization backends, with advanced optimisers like GaLore, BAdam and APOLLO and speed-ups such as FlashAttention-2, Unsloth and Liger Kernel. A hardware table estimates memory needs, from 6 GB for 4-bit QLoRA on a 7B model.

You can train from the CLI with YAML configs, use the LLaMA Board web UI, or run in free cloud notebooks such as Colab. Fine-tuned models can be served with an OpenAI-style API backed by vLLM. Model weights keep their own licenses.
